Congratulations on completing this journey! Job well done!

We hope you've enjoyed traveling with us as you:

- Learned why centralized log aggregation is essential for observability
- Learned about the advantages of using the Loki data source in Grafana Cloud
- Gathered the URL, credentials, and tenant ID for your Loki backend
- Added and named a new Loki data source in Grafana Cloud
- Configured the connection URL for your Loki environment
- Selected an authentication method and entered credentials
- Successfully saved and tested the data source connection
- Verified log data by running a LogQL query in Explore

---

### More to explore (optional)

The world is your oyster! Read more about how you can extend your Loki setup:

- [Derived fields](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources/loki/configure/#derived-fields) — Extract new fields from logs and link to a trace backend.
- [LogQL query language](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/logql/) — Filter, parse, and aggregate your log data.
- [Loki template variables](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources/loki/template-variables/) — Build dynamic dashboards driven by log labels.
- [Provision the Loki data source](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources/loki/configure/#provision-the-data-source) — Manage the data source with a YAML file.
- [Loki best practices](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/best-practices/) — Get the most out of your Loki deployment.

---

### Related paths

Consider taking the following paths after you complete this journey:

- [Use Logs Drilldown to explore your logs](https://grafana.com/docs/learning-paths/drilldown-logs/)
- [Visualize logs in a Grafana Cloud dashboard](https://grafana.com/docs/learning-paths/visualization-logs/)
- [Send logs to Loki with Grafana Alloy](https://grafana.com/docs/learning-paths/send-logs-alloy-loki/)
